t: Owls can't move their eyes in their sockets, so they turn their heads instead — up to about 270 degrees.
Octopuses have three hearts.
Botanically, bananas are berries — but strawberries are not.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Sharks have existed for longer than trees.
Your brain uses about 20% of your body's energy.
A bolt of lightning is about five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Mansa Musa of the Mali Empire is often described as one of the richest people who ever lived.
Wombat poop is cube-shaped.
A group of flamingos is called a "flamboyance".
Hot water can sometimes freeze faster than cold water. It's called the Mpemba effect, after Tanzanian student Erasto Mpemba.
The Sahara is almost as big as the whole United States.
Butterflies taste with their feet.
The shortest war on record, between Britain and Zanzibar in 1896, lasted under an hour.
Africa has 54 countries that are members of the United Nations.
The Great Wall of China cannot be seen from the Moon with the naked eye.
The first email was sent in 1971 by engineer Ray Tomlinson.
Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
Sound travels about four times faster in water than in air.
Polar bears have black skin under their white-looking fur.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
Owls' eyes are tube-shaped rather than round, which helps them see in the dark.
An adult human body holds roughly 5 litres of blood.
Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 15th century, high in Peru's Andes mountains.
The word "robot" comes from the Czech word "robota", meaning forced labour.
Russia spans 11 time zones.
Elephants can recognise themselves in a mirror.
Diamonds and pencil graphite are both made of pure carbon.
The five Olympic rings stand for the five inhabited continents taking part in the Games.
A cheetah can go from standing still to about 100 km/h in roughly three seconds.
Australia is wider than the Moon: about 4,000 km across, against the Moon's 3,474 km.
Lake Baikal in Russia holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh water.
A day on Mars lasts about 24 hours and 40 minutes.
The Rosetta Stone let scholars read Egyptian hieroglyphs because it carries the same text in three scripts.
"Origami" comes from the Japanese words "ori" (folding) and "kami" (paper).
Traditionally, the ancient Olympic Games began in 776 BC in Olympia, Greece.
Giraffes have the same number of neck bones as humans: seven.
Some bamboo species can grow almost a metre in a single day.
Honey never really spoils. Pots of honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs were reportedly still edible.
Studies suggest cows have best friends and get stressed when they are separated.
Sea otters hold hands while they sleep so they don't drift apart.
A hummingbird's heart can beat more than 1,200 times a minute.
Koalas sleep up to 20 hours a day.
An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
Crows can recognise individual human faces and remember them for years.
A blue whale's heart is about the size of a small car.
Starfish have no brain and no blood.
Dolphins give each other names: each one has its own signature whistle.
Penguins live almost only in the Southern Hemisphere.
Some turtles can breathe through their bottoms during winter hibernation.
An owl's feathers have soft, comb-like edges that let it fly almost silently.
There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way, by most estimates.
Water can boil and freeze at the same time at its "triple point".
Your stomach gets a new lining every few days so it doesn't digest itself.
A teaspoon of a neutron star would weigh about a billion tonnes on Earth.
Light from the Sun is about 8 minutes old when it reaches you, but the energy behind it started in the Sun's core tens of thousands of years earlier.
Saturn is so light for its size that it would float in a big enough bathtub.
You are slightly taller in the morning than at night, because the discs in your spine compress during the day.
Glass is made mostly from sand.
The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth, about 3.8 cm every year.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
Oxford University was already teaching students before the Aztec Empire was founded.
The ancient city of Timbuktu in Mali held hundreds of thousands of handwritten manuscripts.
The first known recipe book is from ancient Mesopotamia, written on clay tablets around 1750 BC.
The Great Library of Alexandria tried to collect a copy of every book in the known world.
Paper money was first used in China more than 1,000 years ago.
Canada has more lakes than any other country: over half of the world's large lakes, by some counts.
There's a town in Norway called Hell, and it freezes over most winters.
The Pacific Ocean is wider than the Moon.
Mount Everest grows by a few millimetres every year as the Himalayas keep rising.
The Dead Sea is so salty that people float on it without trying.
Nigeria's Lagos is one of the largest cities in Africa.
The Nile flows north, from East Africa into the Mediterranean Sea.
Antarctica is the largest desert in the world, because it gets so little rain or snow.
Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, smaller than many city parks.
The first computer mouse, built in the 1960s, was made of wood.
The first website ever made is still online at info.cern.ch.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed for typewriters in the 1870s.
The first mobile phone call was made in 1973.
Over half of all web traffic now comes from mobile phones.
The word "bug" for a computer fault became famous after a real moth was found stuck in a computer in 1947.
The first FIFA World Cup was held in Uruguay in 1930.
A golf ball has around 300 to 500 dimples, which help it fly farther.
Basketball was invented in 1891 using a peach basket as the hoop.
Tug of war was an Olympic sport from 1900 to 1920.
Table tennis balls can fly off a bat at over 100 km/h.
The world's most spoken language by total speakers is English; by native speakers, it's Mandarin Chinese.
Africa is home to about a third of the world's languages, more than 2,000 of them.
The "#" symbol is also called an octothorpe.
The dot over a lowercase "i" or "j" is called a tittle.
By tradition, the Bible was written over about 1,500 years by around 40 different authors.
The Book of Psalms has 150 chapters, the most of any book in the Bible.
"Jesus wept" (John 11:35) is the shortest verse in most English Bibles.
The Bible is the most translated book in history; the full Bible is available in over 700 languages.
Methuselah is the oldest person in the Bible: Genesis says he lived 969 years.
The Dead Sea Scrolls, found from 1947, include the oldest known copies of books of the Hebrew Bible.
